paper.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Mathematics in the Natural Sciences
paper.zh_title: 数学在自然科学中不可思议的有效性
paper.author: Eugene P. Wigner
paper.citation: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics, 13(1), February 1960, pp. 1–14. DOI: 10.1002/cpa.3160130102.
paper.description: 抽象数学为什么能如此准确地描述自然？关于数学、物理和解释的经典追问。
paper.note: 本站双语导读，非原文全文或逐句翻译。文章讨论的是数学在自然科学中的有效性，并不宣称每个现象都能被数学完整描述。
paper.rights: 原文章受版权保护，本页仅提供本站编写的双语导读与来源链接。

blocks.en: Wigner asks why mathematics developed through abstract reasoning works so well in describing physical phenomena. The usefulness itself becomes the object of inquiry.
blocks.zh: 维格纳追问：通过抽象推理发展起来的数学，为什么能如此有效地描述物理现象？有效性本身成为了需要解释的问题。

blocks.en: Distinguish fitting a formula to known observations from finding that a mathematical framework reaches further than expected. The latter makes the puzzle especially striking.
blocks.zh: 应当区分两件事：为已知观察拟合一个公式，以及发现某个数学框架适用的范围超出了预期。后一种情形使这个疑问格外鲜明。

blocks.en: This is a conceptual essay, so read its examples as invitations to examine the relationship between mathematical concepts and physical laws. It is not a technical proof of universal mathematical coverage.
blocks.zh: 这是一篇概念性的文章，可以借它的例子考察数学概念与物理定律的关系。它不是一份证明数学能够包揽一切现象的技术证明。

blocks.en: Reading question: does successful prediction fully explain why a model works? Compare practical confidence in a theory with an explanation of its remarkable success.
blocks.zh: 阅读时可以追问：预测成功，是否就完全解释了一个模型为什么有效？可以比较对理论的实用信心，与对其惊人成功的解释。
